text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE

- Defence Minister Shaqir Vukaj, a Socialist, told parliament the Democratic Party had armed its own supporters in March, planned to bomb a key bridge in the south and attempted to incite a north-south division.
- The Interior Ministry will create a special police force for Fieri region in the south.
- Several thousand people in the rebel-held town of Vlore used the visit of exiled king Leka Zogu to hold a protest rally against President Sali Berisha.

- The Socialist Party agreed to a regional proportional elections law whereas the Democrats wanted a nominal system. Smaller parties are happy with a full proportional system but are concerned that the draft does not allow them to the represented in the voting commissions.

- Prime Minister Bashkim Fino assured Herbert Grubmayer, the deputy of OSCE's Albania mission head Franz Vranitzky, that his government of National Reconciliation would take all necessary steps to prepare elections by the end of June.
- A group of Democratic Party MPs and founding members have formed the Movement for Democracy, which they say will revive the original ideals of the ruling Democrats.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- A European tour of Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano was a total failure.
- Defence Minister Shaqir Vukaj and his generals do not have a strategy to build an Albanian army.
- A delegation of the European Democratic Union is expected to visit Albania at the invitation of Democratic Party chairman Tritan Shehu.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- OSCE envoy to Albania Franz Vranitzky says there will be many dangers if elections are postponed. He added Berisha does not want the OSCE to head monitoring of the polls.
- Leka I said he was happy with his visit to Vlore and it was worth going there despite a cool welcome which he attributed to their suffering.

- Socialist leader Fatos Nano says the scrapping of the so-called anti-genocide law which prohibits senior communists from running from office till 2001 will be the first point of debate prior to the elections.
- Special police troops have returned to the southern city of Berat and started operations to collect weapons and fight armed bands.
ALBANIA
- The Tirana court ruled against a demand by Maksude Kadema, the manager of a collapsed pyramid scheme, to be allowed out of jail in order to find the money she owes 10,000 creditors.
- The Albanian revolt is headed by communists and criminals.
- The presence of Alba mission troops has increased safety in Albania.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- OSCE envoy for Albania Franz Vranitzky said he has not scrapped plans to visit the south and north of Albania.
